name: Ariadne
summary: Ariadne, also known chemically as 4C-D or 4C-DOM, by its developmental code name BL-3912, and by its former tentative brand name Dimoxamine, is a non-hallucinogenic psychoactive drug of the phenethylamine, phenylisobutylamine (α-ethylphenethylamine), and 4C families.

pharmacology.text: Ariadne is a potent and selective agonist of the serotonin 5-HT2 receptors, including of the serotonin 5-HT2A, 5-HT2B, and 5-HT2C receptors. However, it is less efficacious in activating the serotonin 5-HT2A receptor, including the Gq, G11, and β-arrestin2 signaling pathways, compared to the related drug DOM, and this weaker partial agonism may be responsible for its lack of psychedelic effects.
pharmacology.kind: Serotonin 5-HT2A, 5-HT2B, and 5-HT2C receptor agonist; Non-hallucinogenic serotonin 5-HT2A receptor agonist; Antidepressant; Stimulant

uses.text: It was developed as a potential pharmaceutical drug at Bristol Laboratories, for instance as an antidepressant and for various other uses, and entered clinical trials around 1974. The development of Ariadne is said to have been discontinued for strategic economic reasons rather than due to issues with effectiveness or safety.

sideEffects.en: It activates the 5-HT2A receptor only weakly and was reported not to cause hallucinations. Its effects in people are little documented beyond those old trials, so its risks are not well known.
sideEffects.zh: 它只微弱地活化 5-HT2A 受體，據報告不會造成幻覺。除了那些舊試驗之外，它對人體的作用紀錄很少，因此風險並不清楚。
sideEffects.zhHans: 它只微弱地活化 5-HT2A 受体，据报告不会造成幻觉。除了那些旧试验之外，它对人体的作用纪录很少，因此风险并不清楚。

fact.en: Ariadne is named after the figure from Greek myth who gave Theseus the thread out of the labyrinth. Alexander Shulgin worked on it at Bristol Laboratories, and it entered clinical trials around 1974 as a possible medicine.
fact.zh: Ariadne 的名稱來自希臘神話中給忒修斯線團走出迷宮的人物。Alexander Shulgin 曾在 Bristol Laboratories 研究它，它約在 1974 年作為可能的藥物進入臨床試驗。
fact.zhHans: Ariadne 的名称来自希腊神话中给忒修斯线团走出迷宫的人物。Alexander Shulgin 曾在 Bristol Laboratories 研究它，它约在 1974 年作为可能的药物进入临床试验。
